results.fulltext: Pursuant to section 86(4)(b) of the Immigration Act 2009, I, Hon Erica Stanford, Minister of Immigration, make the following special direction, which suspends the waiver of the requirement to hold a transit visa to travel to and be in New Zealand only as a transit passenger, for nationals of Kuwait. Special Direction 1. Title This special direction may be cited as the Suspending Transit Visa Waiver Status for Nationals of Kuwait Special Direction 2026. 2. Commencement This special direction comes into force at 11.59pm on 12 November 2026 . 3. Suspension of Transit Visa Waiver In accordance with section 86(4)(b), I suspend the waiver of the requirement to hold a transit visa to travel to and be in New Zealand only as a transit passenger, provided under Regulation 16, item 12(y) of Schedule 1 and item 8(26) of Schedule 2 of the Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 in respect of all: citizens of Kuwait; and persons travelling on a passport issued by Kuwait 4. Period of Suspension The suspension takes effect from 11.59pm on 12 November 2026 and expires at 11.59pm on 11 February 2027 , being a period of three months. 5. Effect of Suspension During the period of suspension, every person to whom this special direction applies must hold a valid transit visa before travelling to New Zealand for the purpose of transiting through New Zealand, unless exempted from that requirement under the Immigration Act 2009 or any other applicable enactment. 6. Notification This special direction must be notified through diplomatic channels to the Government of Kuwait. It must be published in the New Zealand Gazette and presented to the House of Representatives. Dated at Wellington this 4th day of November 2026. Hon ERICA STANFORD, Minister of Immigration. Explanatory Note This special direction suspends, for a period of three months, the transit visa waiver arrangements that would otherwise apply to citizens of Kuwait and persons travelling on passports issued by Kuwait. During the suspension period, affected persons must obtain a transit visa before travelling to New Zealand for the purpose of transiting through New Zealand. The special direction is made under section 86(4)(b) of the Immigration Act 2009. The direction expires three months after it takes effect, unless sooner revoked. Provisions of the Regulatory Standards Act 2025 set requirements for explanatory notes that apply to secondary legislation made after 1 July 2026. Section 14 of the Regulatory Standards Act 2025 requires the responsible agency for secondary legislation to ensure that an explanatory note for the secondary legislation includes (or contains a link to): a consistency accountability statement (CAS); a statement from the maker that briefly explains the maker’s reasons for any inconsistency with the principles of responsible regulation that is identified in the consistency accountability statement. Cabinet Office Circular CO (26) 2 also requires responsible agencies subject to Cabinet direction to publish a summary of underpinning analysis that supports the CAS. Special Direction 1. Title This special direction may be cited as the Suspending Visa Waiver Status for Nationals of Kuwait Special Direction 2026. 2. Commencement This special direction comes into force at 11.59pm on 12 November 2026 . 3. Suspension of Visa Waiver In accordance with section 69(2)(b), I suspend the waiver of the requirement to hold a visa permitting travel to New Zealand provided under Regulation 18(1) and item 8(26) of Schedule 2 of the Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 in respect of: all citizens of Kuwait who are seeking entry permission and a temporary visa that is current for no more than 3 months and the purpose of the visit does not include medical consultation and treatment; and all persons travelling on a passport issued by Kuwait who are seeking entry permission and a temporary visa that is current for no more than 3 months and the purpose of the visit does not include medical consultation and treatment. 4. Period of Suspension The suspension takes effect at 11.59pm on 12 November 2026 and expires at 11.59pm on 11 February 2027 , being a period of three months. 5. Effect of Suspension During the period of suspension, persons to whom this direction applies must hold a visa permitting travel to New Zealand before commencing travel to New Zealand, unless otherwise exempt under the Immigration Act 2009 or any other applicable enactment. 6. Notification This special direction must be notified through diplomatic channels to the Government of Kuwait in accordance with section 69(4)(a). It must be published in the New Zealand Gazette and presented to the House of Representatives. Dated at Wellington this 4th day of November 2026. Hon ERICA STANFORD, Minister of Immigration. Explanatory Note This special direction suspends, for a period of three months, the waiver of the requirement to hold a visa permitting travel to New Zealand that would otherwise apply to citizens of Kuwait and persons travelling on passports issued by Kuwait. The direction is made under section 69(2)(b) of the Immigration Act 2009. Note: Section 69(4)(b) provides that a special direction of this type expires after three months (or any shorter period specified), unless sooner cancelled. Its reference number is CIV-2026-404-749. The application is to be heard by the High Court at Auckland on Thursday, 26 November 2026 at 10.45am. A person, other than the defendant company, who wants to appear at the hearing of the application must file an appearance not later than the second working day before that day. The statement of claim and the verifying affidavit may be inspected at the registry of the court or at the plaintiff’s address for service. The plaintiff is the Commissioner of Inland Revenue , whose address for service is Inland Revenue, Legal Services, 5 Osterley Way, Manukau City, Auckland 2104. The plaintiff’s solicitor is Hosanna Tanielu, whose address is as noted above. Dated this 11th day of November 2026.
